newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht edges higher late, interbank rate eases.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht edges higher late, interbank rate eases.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed against the dollar late on Wednesday in the onshore market as dollar demand by importers eased, dealers said.
There was no apparent central bank intervention, they said.
"The baht was a little bit stronger in the afternoon. There was no apparent sign of central bank's intervention today, but dollar demand by importers was easing," said one local dealer.
The dealer said the baht was still trading around 30 baht, which is seen as a very strong resistance level.
The baht was quoted at 29.95/30.00 per dollar late in onshore market compared with 30.11/30.20 in the morning.
The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday announced that the weighted average interbank exchange rate was 29.967 per dollar against 30.348 on Tuesday.
In the offshore market, the baht was quoted at 29.80/29.90 late against 30.00/30.20 in the morning.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was traded at 30/35 satangs per dollar late in the domestic market and 70/90 in the offshore market.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 17.50-18.00 percent late from 19.00-20.00 percent in the morning on rising liquidity, dealers said. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
